title: IPO
summary: You may complete at most k distinct projects.

contractDetails.constraints: 1 ≤ k ≤ 100000. There are 1–100000 projects, and the profits and capital arrays have equal length. 0 ≤ w,capital[i] ≤ 1000000000. 0 ≤ profits[i] ≤ 10000. The result fits signed 32-bit range.
contractDetails.output-checking: Compare the optimum final integer capital. A project may be used at most once and capital thresholds are eligibility tests, not deductions.

statement: You may complete at most k distinct projects. Project i can start when your current capital is at least capital[i]. Finishing it adds profits[i] to your capital without subtracting the eligibility threshold. Return the greatest final capital obtainable from initial capital w.

examples.explanation: First gain 2, then gain 5. Eligibility thresholds are not expenses.
At most two distinct projects exist, including a zero-profit one.

constraints: 1 ≤ k ≤ 100000. There are 1–100000 projects, and the profits and capital arrays have equal length. 0 ≤ w,capital[i] ≤ 1000000000. 0 ≤ profits[i] ≤ 10000. The result fits signed 32-bit range.
hints: Conceptual: Finishing a feasible project may unlock more projects.
Directional: Separate the question of affordability from the question of best profit.
Implementation: Move affordable projects from a capital-ordered structure to a profit max-heap. Complete its best project and repeat, stopping when no project is available.

expectedComplexity.time: O(n log n + k log n)
expectedComplexity.space: O(n log n + k log n)

complexityAnalysis: O(n log n + k log n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.
